classification.difficultyReason: Decompose the overlap into two segments and use perpendicular chord bisectors to obtain their central angles from half the chord before applying the taught segment formula.

inlines.text: The diagram below shows two intersecting circles, of radius 5 and 4. The length between the points of intersection is 6.
Find the common area where the circles overlap, correct to one decimal place.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 33, lower right column, printed page 277
spec.description: Smaller circle on the left and larger circle on the right, with marked centres, dashed radii labelled 4 and 5, a vertical common chord labelled 6, and a shaded overlap lens.
spec.mathematics: Place the common chord endpoints at (0,3) and (0,-3). The radius-4 centre is (-sqrt(7),0), and the radius-5 centre is (4,0), so both circles pass through both endpoints and their centres lie on opposite sides of the chord.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens and requested region are visible. No central angles, half-chord values or area answers are supplied.

inlines.text: Halve the common chord to find each central angle, then add the two segment areas.

answer.worked:
The perpendicular from each centre bisects the common chord, so each half has length $3$. Let $\theta_4$ and $\theta_5$ be the central angles subtended by the chord in the circles of radii $4$ and $5$, respectively. In radians,
$$\begin{align*}
\theta_4 &= 2\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\\
\theta_5 &= 2\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{3}{5}\right).
\end{align*}$$
Each segment area is the sector area minus the triangle area:
$$\begin{align*}
A_4 &= \frac12(4)^2(\theta_4-\sin\theta_4)\\
A_4 &= 16\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac34\right)-3\sqrt7\\
A_5 &= \frac12(5)^2(\theta_5-\sin\theta_5)\\
A_5 &= 25\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac35\right)-12.
\end{align*}$$
The overlap consists of these two segments:
$$\begin{align*}
A &= A_4+A_5\\
A &= 16\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac34\right)+25\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac35\right)-3\sqrt7-12\\
A &\approx 9.7\text{ square units}\quad\text{(1 decimal place)}.
\end{align*}$$
